correctness.rationale: For each m>=1 the first/last differing positions in equal-length palindromes are symmetric. Common one-deletion descendants force their centered differing interval to alternate with complementary phases, and deleting its opposite endpoints proves the converse. Even-length centers contain equal symbols so no nontrivial alternating interval exists. For odd length 2m-1 the halfword edge criterion is exactly a complementary alternating tail. Recursive separation by first bit produces two rooted copies joined by their alternating-root edge, a binomial tree with 2^m vertices. A last-bit perfect matching bounds independence by 2^(m-1); tree bipartition attains it. Rooted maximum-independent-set recurrence N_m=N_(m-1)^2-A_(m-1)^2, A_m=A_(m-1)(N_(m-1)-A_(m-1)), with N_1=2,A_1=1 yields N_m=(m+1)prod_{j=1}^{m-1}j^{2^(m-1-j)}. Independently constructed deletion shadows and alternating-tail predicted graph for m=1..6: every odd edge agrees; even graphs empty. Finite m checks corroborate the all-m proof.
